preamble:
This process's open-descriptor count, and the bound a run of compiles holds it to, with its leaking negative control (gh-ocannl-1784, gh-ocannl-1882).

This process's open descriptors, and the bound a run of compiles holds them to (gh-ocannl-1784, gh-ocannl-1882).

A debug-artifact writer that keeps its descriptor past its write leaks one or more per compile, and only a long run under a low limit (macOS's 256 in a non-interactive ssh shell) notices. build_file_descriptors pins the contract on a trivial routine, and schedule_mma_matmul, the longest compile-heavy test, holds every writer its routines reach to it. Both read the same counter and claim the same bound. Each test's negative control leaks a channel count the test writes as its own literal, independent of bound, and claims the bound rejects it: so a counter that cannot see growth fails the control, and so does a bound loosened past that count. schedule_mma_matmul also claims the bound, its baseline and its control fit under low_shell_limit.

Each test makes its claims in its own Verdict.leg, closed on Windows, which has no /dev/fd (built at the claim's site, where verdict_ratchet's gate reader follows it): the readings there are 0, and only the skipped claims would read them.
content:
val count : unit -> int

The number of this process's open descriptors. /dev/fd lists them on macOS and Linux; the listing's own descriptor is counted in every reading alike.

val low_shell_limit : int

The descriptor limit of a non-interactive ssh shell on macOS, under which schedule_mma_matmul once ran out of descriptors (gh-ocannl-1784).

val allowance : int

The most new descriptors any number of compiles may leave open: the room for one-time state opened on demand after the warm-up compile -- driver state a routine's first compile or launch of a new kind opens, and that stays open for the process's lifetime. On cc and Metal that state measured nothing (the tests print their growth on stderr); the room is for backends where it was not measured (CUDA and HIP), and it stays far below low_shell_limit.

val bound : compiles:Base.Int.t -> Base.Int.t

bound ~compiles is the number of new open descriptors compiles compiles, read after a warm-up compile, must stay below: one per compile up to allowance. Every artifact writer runs on every compile of its backend, so a writer that keeps even one descriptor breaks it once the run has allowance compiles, and a short run breaks it from its first leaked descriptor per compile; a leak only some compiles reach breaks it once it has leaked allowance.

val within_bound : compiles:Base.Int.t -> int -> bool

within_bound ~compiles growth is growth < bound ~compiles.

val leak_growth : int -> Base__Int.t

leak_growth n keeps n channels open at once, reads the growth through count and closes them: the negative control's measurement. n must be positive, since a control that leaks nothing shows nothing.
